question.text: A tuning fork resonates with a sonometer wire of length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> stretched with a tension of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo>.</mo></math> When the tension in the wire is changed to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>54</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo>,</mo></math> the same tuning fork produces <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>12</mn></math> beats per second with it. The frequency of the tuning fork is _______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Hz</mi><mo>.</mo></math>

solution.text:
Frequency of sonometer wire is given by, f=12 LTμ

Therefore, f1=126μ f2=1254μ

Hence, f1f2=13 

Also it is given that, f2-f1=12

So, f1=6 Hz.
